In probability theory and statistics, the '''half-normal distribution''' is a special case of the [[folded normal distribution]].

Let <math>X</math> follow an ordinary [[normal distribution]], <math>N(0,\sigma^2)</math>. Then, <math>Y=|X|</math> follows a half-normal distribution. Thus, the half-normal distribution is a fold at the mean of an ordinary normal distribution with mean zero.

==Properties==

Using the <math>\sigma</math> parametrization of the normal distribution, the [[probability density function]] (PDF) of the half-normal is given by

: <math>f_Y(y; \sigma) = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sigma\sqrt{\pi}}\exp \left( -\frac{y^2}{2\sigma^2} \right) \quad y \geq 0,</math>

where <math>E[Y] = \mu = \frac{\sigma\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{\pi}}</math>.

Alternatively using a scaled precision (inverse of the variance) parametrization (to avoid issues if <math>\sigma</math> is near zero), obtained by setting <math>\theta=\frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{\sigma\sqrt{2}}</math>, the [[probability density function]] is given by

: <math>f_Y(y; \theta) = \frac{2\theta}{\pi}\exp  \left( -\frac{y^2\theta^2}{\pi} \right) \quad y \geq 0,</math>

where <math>E[Y] = \mu = \frac{1}{\theta}</math>.

The [[cumulative distribution function]] (CDF) is given by

: <math>F_Y(y; \sigma) = \int_0^y \frac{1}{\sigma}\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \, \exp \left( -\frac{x^2}{2\sigma^2} \right)\, dx</math>

Using the change-of-variables <math>z = x/(\sqrt{2}\sigma)</math>, the CDF can be written as

: <math>F_Y(y; \sigma) = \frac{2}{\sqrt{\pi}} \,\int_0^{y/(\sqrt{2}\sigma)}\exp \left(-z^2\right)dz  = \operatorname{erf}\left(\frac{y}{\sqrt{2}\sigma}\right),
</math>
where erf is the [[error function]], a standard function in many mathematical software packages.

The quantile function (or inverse CDF) is written:
:<math>Q(F;\sigma)=\sigma\sqrt{2} \operatorname{erf}^{-1}(F)</math>
where <math>0\le F \le 1</math> and <math>\operatorname{erf}^{-1}</math> is the [[Inverse error function#Inverse functions|inverse error function]]

The expectation is then given by

: <math>E[Y] = \sigma \sqrt{2/\pi},</math>

The variance is given by

: <math>\operatorname{var}(Y) = \sigma^2\left(1 - \frac{2}{\pi}\right). </math>

Since this is proportional to the variance σ<sup>2</sup> of ''X'', ''σ'' can be seen as a [[scale parameter]] of the new distribution.

The differential entropy of the half-normal distribution is exactly one bit less the differential entropy of a zero-mean normal distribution with the same second moment about&nbsp;0. This can be understood intuitively since the magnitude operator reduces information by one bit (if the probability distribution at its input is even). Alternatively, since a half-normal distribution is always positive, the one bit it would take to record whether a standard normal random variable were positive (say, a 1) or negative (say, a 0) is no longer necessary. Thus,

: <math> h(Y) = \frac{1}{2}  \log_2 \left( \frac{\pi e \sigma^2}{2} \right) = \frac{1}{2}  \log_2 \left( 2\pi e \sigma^2 \right) -1.</math>

==Applications==

The half-normal distribution is commonly utilized as a [[prior probability distribution]] for [[variance]] parameters in [[Bayesian inference]] applications.<ref>{{Citation | last=Gelman | first=A. | title=Prior distributions for variance parameters in hierarchical models | journal=Bayesian Analysis | year=2006 | volume=1 | issue=3 | pages=515–534 | doi=10.1214/06-ba117a| doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Citation | last1=Röver | first1=C. | last2=Bender | first2=R. | last3=Dias | first3=S. | last4=Schmid | first4=C.H. | last5=Schmidli | first5=H. | last6=Sturtz | first6=S. | last7=Weber | first7=S. | last8=Friede | first8=T. | title=On weakly informative prior distributions for the heterogeneity parameter in Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis | journal=Research Synthesis Methods | year=2021 | volume=12 | issue=4 | pages=448–474 | doi=10.1002/jrsm.1475 | pmid=33486828 | arxiv=2007.08352| s2cid=220546288 }}</ref>

== Parameter estimation ==

Given numbers <math>\{x_i\}_{i=1}^n</math> drawn from a half-normal distribution, the unknown parameter <math>\sigma</math> of that distribution can be estimated by the method of [[maximum likelihood]], giving

: <math> \hat \sigma = \sqrt{\frac 1 n \sum_{i=1}^n x_i^2}</math>

The bias is equal to 
: <math>
    b \equiv \operatorname{E}\bigg[\;(\hat\sigma_\mathrm{mle} - \sigma)\;\bigg]
        = - \frac{\sigma}{4n} 
  </math>

which yields the [[Maximum_likelihood_estimation#Higher-order_properties|bias-corrected maximum likelihood estimator]]

: <math>
    \hat{\sigma\,}^*_\text{mle} = \hat{\sigma\,}_\text{mle} - \hat{b\,}.
  </math>

== Related distributions ==

* The distribution is a special case of the [[folded normal distribution]] with ''μ''&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.
* It also coincides with a zero-mean normal distribution truncated from below at zero (see [[truncated normal distribution]])
* If ''Y'' has a half-normal distribution, then (''Y''/''σ'')<sup>2</sup> has a [[chi square distribution]] with 1 degree of freedom, i.e. ''Y''/''σ'' has a [[chi distribution]] with 1 degree of freedom.
* The half-normal distribution is a special case of the [[generalized gamma distribution]] with ''d''&nbsp;=&nbsp;1, ''p''&nbsp;=&nbsp;2, ''a''&nbsp;=&nbsp;<math>\sqrt{2}\sigma</math>.
* If ''Y'' has a half-normal distribution, ''Y''<sup> -2</sup> has a [[Lévy distribution]]
* The [[Rayleigh  distribution]] is a moment-tilted and scaled generalization of the half-normal distribution.
